html:
The railway, completed in 1869, that linked the existing rail network of the eastern United States to the Pacific coast. It cut the journey across the country from months by wagon or ship to about a week.

Congress approved it in 1862, during the Civil War, with land grants and loans. Two companies built it toward each other:

  • The Central Pacific built east from Sacramento, California, through the granite of the Sierra Nevada. Most of its workers were Chinese immigrants, who did the hardest and most dangerous work for less pay.
  • The Union Pacific built west from Omaha across the plains, with many Irish workers and Civil War veterans.

They met at Promontory Summit, Utah, on 10 May 1869, where a golden spike was driven.

The railway opened the West to fast settlement and trade. It also sped the slaughter of the bison and the loss of Native lands. Chinese workers got little thanks; within years came the Chinese Exclusion Act. Canada built its own line, the Canadian Pacific Railway, in the 1880s.
